Use grammar and structures accurately; items marked (R) need only receptive knowledge.
Know the AS grammar list.
Use noun gender, singular and plural forms, case marking and weak masculine nouns.
Use definite and indefinite articles (including kein), demonstratives, possessives and other determiners.
Use personal, reflexive, relative, demonstrative, possessive, indefinite and interrogative pronouns.
Use adjective endings, comparatives and superlatives, adjectives with dative and with prepositions.
Use adverbs and adverbials of time, place, direction, manner, degree and question.
Use comparative and superlative adverbs, numbers, fractions, clock time, days and months.
Use modal particles and discourse markers such as ja, doch, wohl.
Use principal parts of weak, strong and irregular verbs.
Use reflexive, separable and inseparable verbs.
Use haben, sein and werden, and choose haben or sein in the perfect.
Use modal verbs in present and imperfect, and the imperfect subjunctive of mögen and können.
Use infinitive constructions: um...zu, ohne...zu, verbs with zu, lassen and sich lassen.
Use present, imperfect, perfect and pluperfect tenses.
Use the future, conditional and passive with werden, and the imperative.
Use the past subjunctive in conditional clauses.
Recognise perfect modals, future perfect, conditional perfect, pluperfect subjunctive and indirect-speech subjunctive (receptive).
Use fixed-case and dual-case prepositions and prepositional adverbs such as darauf.
Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
Use the nominative, accusative and dative objects, prepositional objects and copular verbs.
Use main clause word order, questions, commands, and positions of pronouns, adverbials and nicht.
Vary word order for emphasis.
Use subordinate clauses introduced by conjunctions such as dass and obwohl.
Form compound nouns, nouns from verbs and adjectives, and verbs from nouns and adjectives.
Use separable and inseparable prefixes.
Know the A-level additions to the AS grammar list.
Recognise long adjective phrases (receptive).
Use perfect modals, future perfect and conditional perfect.
Recognise conditional sentences with omitted wenn (receptive).
Use the passive with sein and the pluperfect subjunctive in conditional clauses.
Use all forms of indirect speech.
Recognise the prepositional adverb anticipating dass and infinitive clauses (receptive).
